# REST version of Spring PetClinic Sample Application (spring-framework-petclinic extension)

[![Java Build Status](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/maven-build-master.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/maven-build-master.yml)
[![Docker Build Status](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/docker-build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/docker-build.yml)
[![Quality Gate Status](https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_badges/measure?project=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest&metric=alert_status)](https://sonarcloud.io/dashboard?id=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest)
[![Coverage](https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_badges/measure?project=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest&metric=coverage)](https://sonarcloud.io/dashboard?id=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest)

This backend version of the Spring Petclinic application only provides a REST API. **There is no UI**.
The [spring-petclinic-angular project](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-angular) is a Angular front-end application which consumes the REST API.

## Understanding the Spring Petclinic application with a few diagrams

[See the presentation of the Spring Petclinic Framework version](http://fr.slideshare.net/AntoineRey/spring-framework-petclinic-sample-application)

### Petclinic ER Model

![alt petclinic-ermodel](petclinic-ermodel.png)

## Running Petclinic locally

### With Maven command line
```sh
git clone https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest.git
cd spring-petclinic-rest
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

### With Docker
```sh
docker run -p 9966:9966 springcommunity/spring-petclinic-rest
```

package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation;

import java.util.Map;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.mapper.OwnerMapper;

/**
 * Validates optional owner postcodes against the postcode range of the owner's city region.
 */
public final class OwnerPostcode {

    private static final Pattern FOUR_DIGITS = Pattern.compile("^[0-9]{4}$");

    /** Inclusive postcode range per region, keyed by the regions of {@link OwnerMapper#CITY_REGIONS}. */
    public static final Map<String, int[]> RANGES_BY_REGION = Map.of(
        "NSW", new int[] {2000, 2099},
        "VIC", new int[] {3000, 3099},
        "QLD", new int[] {4000, 4099});

    /** The region of owners whose postcode and city match no known region. */
    public static final String UNKNOWN_REGION = "UNKNOWN";

    private OwnerPostcode() {
    }

    /**
     * The owner's region: the region whose range contains the postcode; when the postcode is absent or
     * in no known range, the region of the city from {@link OwnerMapper#CITY_REGIONS}, or
     * {@value #UNKNOWN_REGION} when the city is not listed.
     *
     * @param postcode the postcode, may be {@code null}
     * @param city the city, may be {@code null}
     * @return the region, never {@code null}
     */
    public static String regionOf(String postcode, String city) {
        String postcodeRegion = regionOf(postcode);
        if (postcodeRegion != null) {
            return postcodeRegion;
        }
        return city == null ? UNKNOWN_REGION : OwnerMapper.CITY_REGIONS.getOrDefault(city, UNKNOWN_REGION);
    }

    /**
     * The region whose range in {@link #RANGES_BY_REGION} contains the postcode.
     *
     * @param postcode the postcode, may be {@code null}
     * @return the region, or {@code null} when the postcode is absent, not 4 digits or in no known range
     */
    public static String regionOf(String postcode) {
        if (postcode == null || !FOUR_DIGITS.matcher(postcode).matches()) {
            return null;
        }
        int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode);
        for (Map.Entry<String, int[]> entry : RANGES_BY_REGION.entrySet()) {
            if (value >= entry.getValue()[0] && value <= entry.getValue()[1]) {
                return entry.getKey();
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Checks a postcode for the given city. An absent postcode is accepted; a present one must be
     * 4 digits and, when the city has a known region, lie within that region's range.
     *
     * @param postcode the postcode as supplied in the request, may be {@code null}
     * @param city the owner's city
     * @throws InvalidPostcodeException if the postcode is malformed or out of range for the city's region
     */
    public static void validate(String postcode, String city) {
        if (postcode == null) {
            return;
        }
        if (!FOUR_DIGITS.matcher(postcode).matches()) {
            throw new InvalidPostcodeException(postcode, "Postcode must be 4 digits");
        }
        String region = city == null ? null : OwnerMapper.CITY_REGIONS.get(city);
        int[] range = region == null ? null : RANGES_BY_REGION.get(region);
        if (range == null) {
            return;
        }
        int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode);
        if (value < range[0] || value > range[1]) {
            throw new InvalidPostcodeException(postcode, "Postcode for " + city + " (" + region
                + ") must be between " + range[0] + " and " + range[1]);
        }
    }
}

package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation;

import java.util.Map;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.mapper.OwnerMapper;

/**
 * Validates optional owner postcodes against the postcode range of the owner's city region.
 */
public final class OwnerPostcode {

    private static final Pattern FOUR_DIGITS = Pattern.compile("^[0-9]{4}$");

    /** Inclusive postcode range per region, keyed by the regions of {@link OwnerMapper#CITY_REGIONS}. */
    public static final Map<String, int[]> RANGES_BY_REGION = Map.of(
        "NSW", new int[] {2000, 2099},
        "VIC", new int[] {3000, 3099},
        "QLD", new int[] {4000, 4099});

    /** The region of owners whose postcode and city match no known region. */
    public static final String UNKNOWN_REGION = "UNKNOWN";

    private OwnerPostcode() {
    }

    /**
     * The owner's region: the region whose range contains the postcode; when the postcode is absent or
     * in no known range, the region of the city from {@link OwnerMapper#CITY_REGIONS}, or
     * {@value #UNKNOWN_REGION} when the city is not listed.
     *
     * @param postcode the postcode, may be {@code null}
     * @param city the city, may be {@code null}
     * @return the region, never {@code null}
     */
    public static String regionOf(String postcode, String city) {
        String postcodeRegion = regionOf(postcode);
        if (postcodeRegion != null) {
            return postcodeRegion;
        }
        return city == null ? UNKNOWN_REGION : OwnerMapper.CITY_REGIONS.getOrDefault(city, UNKNOWN_REGION);
    }

    /**
     * The region whose range in {@link #RANGES_BY_REGION} contains the postcode.
     *
     * @param postcode the postcode, may be {@code null}
     * @return the region, or {@code null} when the postcode is absent, not 4 digits or in no known range
     */
    public static String regionOf(String postcode) {
        if (postcode == null || !FOUR_DIGITS.matcher(postcode).matches()) {
            return null;
        }
        int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode);
        for (Map.Entry<String, int[]> entry : RANGES_BY_REGION.entrySet()) {
            if (value >= entry.getValue()[0] && value <= entry.getValue()[1]) {
                return entry.getKey();
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Checks a postcode for the given city. An absent postcode is accepted; a present one must be
     * 4 digits and, when the city has a known region, lie within that region's range.
     *
     * @param postcode the postcode as supplied in the request, may be {@code null}
     * @param city the owner's city
     * @throws InvalidPostcodeException if the postcode is malformed or out of range for the city's region
     */
    public static void validate(String postcode, String city) {
        if (postcode == null) {
            return;
        }
        if (!FOUR_DIGITS.matcher(postcode).matches()) {
            throw new InvalidPostcodeException(postcode, "Postcode must be 4 digits");
        }
        String region = city == null ? null : OwnerMapper.CITY_REGIONS.get(city);
        int[] range = region == null ? null : RANGES_BY_REGION.get(region);
        if (range == null) {
            return;
        }
        int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode);
        if (value < range[0] || value > range[1]) {
            throw new InvalidPostcodeException(postcode, "Postcode for " + city + " (" + region
                + ") must be between " + range[0] + " and " + range[1]);
        }
    }
}

            is rejected with 400 Bad Request.
          type: string

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner, stored and returned in E.164 form. Spaces,
            dashes and brackets are removed. A leading '+' and country code are kept; otherwise
            a single leading '0' is dropped and country code '+61' is assumed. Between 8 and 15
            digits must follow the '+', e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678'. Numbers
            with country code '+61' must have exactly 9 national digits and numbers with country
            code '+1' exactly 10.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a syntactically
            valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased. An address at a disposable
            email domain (mailinator.com, tempmail.com, guerrillamail.com, or a subdomain of one)
            is rejected with 400 Bad Request.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be valid for the
            region of the owner's city per the fixed table NSW (Sydney) 2000-2099, VIC (Melbourne)
            3000-3099, QLD (Brisbane) 4000-4099; a postcode outside its city's range is rejected
            with 400 Bad Request. A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          minLength: 4
          maxLength: 4
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner registered with the clinic. On create, when omitted it defaults to
            the server's current date. A Saturday or Sunday (supplied or defaulted) is rolled
            forward to the following Monday. A supplied date later than the server's current date
            is rejected with 400 Bad Request.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, used to derive 'ageBand'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Set to true on create to declare that the new owner shares the household of existing
            owners with the same last name and postcode (see 'householdId'). Without it, creating an
            owner whose household already has members is rejected with 409 Conflict; with it, the
            owner is created as a household member and is not flagged as a possible duplicate. It
            does not affect the 'householdId' itself. Not stored.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false

              readOnly: true
            initials:

              description: The upper-cased first letters of the owner's first and last names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                Assigned on create as '<REGION>-<HASH8>': the region whose postcode range contains
                the postcode (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099; when the postcode is absent
                or in no range, the region of the city as for 'locality', otherwise 'UNKNOWN'), a dash,
                and the first 8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the
                normalized telephone followed by the last name.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-3FA9C27B'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                The Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in 'customerCode',
                ignoring all non-digit characters. Absent when the owner has no customer code.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 6
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                Deterministic identifier shared by owners in the same household: the first 12
                lower-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of '<lastName>|<postcode>', with the last
                name trimmed, whitespace-collapsed and lower-cased. Owners with the same last name and
                postcode therefore always share it. Absent for owners without a postcode.
              type: string
              example: '3f2b8c1e7a4d'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                Derived identity used for duplicate detection, formatted as
                '<telephone>|<email>|<householdId>' from the normalized telephone, the lower-cased
                email (empty when absent) and the household ID (empty when absent). Creating an owner
                whose whole identity key equals an existing owner's is rejected with 409 Conflict;
                owners differing in any part, e.g. household members with different telephones, are
                allowed.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|'
              readOnly: true

              title: Namesake count
              description: >-

                created with the same first name and last name, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 0
              readOnly: true

                registration date's year, e.g. 'NSW-3FA9C27B-M26'. Absent when the owner has no
                customer code or registration date.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-3FA9C27B-M20'
              readOnly: true

              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                Assigned on create: starts at 0, plus 2 when an email is present, plus 1 when
                'namesakeCount' is 0, plus 2 when the owner's household has 3 or more members
                (including the owner), plus 3 for a tenure of more than 365 days. A newly created
                owner has zero tenure, so it never earns the tenure points.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true

              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                Derived from 'membershipPoints': 1 for 0-1 points, 2 for 2-3 points, 3 for 4-5
                points, 4 for 6 or more points.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true

              title: Locality
              description: >-

                whose postcode range contains the postcode, otherwise the region derived from the city
                using the fixed table Sydney -> 'NSW', Melbourne -> 'VIC', Brisbane -> 'QLD';
                'UNKNOWN' for any other city.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true

- **`OwnerMapper`:** builds `salutation` from the title and last name.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.updateOwner`:** an update replaces the title. Unlike birth date, leaving it out of a PUT clears the title rather than keeping the old one.

There's no test for the no-title case (salutation is just the last name). It's a one-line branch, but I can add a test for it if you want.
